question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Battle of St. Thome — basic facts and geography]
options: Battle of St. Thome — fought near the Adyar River, south of Madras
French commander at St. Thome — Paradis led the French infantry
Nawab of the Carnatic at the time — Anwaruddin Khan opposed the French advance
St. Thome — a Portuguese settlement located north of the River Cooum inside Madras
wrong_fact: St. Thome (São Tomé) is located south of central Madras, between the Cooum and Adyar Rivers, not north of the Cooum. The battle was fought near the Adyar River to the south.
explanation: The Battle of St. Thome (November 1746) was fought near the Adyar River, south of central Madras. French forces under Paradis routed the far larger army of Nawab Anwaruddin Khan. St. Thome is a historic Portuguese settlement situated between the Cooum and Adyar Rivers — it lies south of central Madras, not north of the Cooum.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Significance and context of the Battle of St. Thome, 1746]
options: Nawab Anwaruddin's force — estimated at ~10,000 soldiers against ~400 French troops
Outcome — French infantry under Paradis decisively defeated the Nawab's larger army
Strategic impact — demonstrated European military superiority over Indian armies in open battle
Location of the battle — the banks of the Krishna River near its delta in the Northern Circars
wrong_fact: The Battle of St. Thome was fought near the Adyar River south of Madras, not near the Krishna River. The Krishna delta and Northern Circars are hundreds of kilometres north of Madras.
explanation: At St. Thome, roughly 400 French troops under Paradis routed an Indian force estimated at around 10,000. The battle was fought near the Adyar River south of Madras — a landmark lesson in European tactical firepower and discipline. The Krishna River delta (Northern Circars) is far to the north and was unrelated to this engagement.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Geo-political aftermath of the Battle of St. Thome]
options: Nawab Anwaruddin Khan — ruler of Arcot who was killed at the later Battle of Ambur (1749), not at St. Thome
Muzaffar Jung — claimant to the Hyderabad throne who later allied with Dupleix after St. Thome emboldened French ambitions
Trichinopoly (Tiruchirappalli) — city that became a key contested point in subsequent Carnatic Wars
Srirangapatna — the island fortress near Madras that the French fortified immediately after their St. Thome victory
wrong_fact: Srirangapatna is located on an island in the Kaveri River near Mysore (modern Karnataka), far from Madras. The French did not fortify it after St. Thome; it was the capital of the Kingdom of Mysore, later associated with Hyder Ali and Tipu Sultan.
explanation: After the Battle of St. Thome, the French held Madras and their victory emboldened Dupleix's political ambitions. Anwaruddin Khan was later killed at Ambur (1749). Muzaffar Jung became a French ally in the Deccan intrigues. Trichinopoly became the central flashpoint of the Second Carnatic War. Srirangapatna (Seringapatam) is on an island in the Kaveri near Mysore — entirely unconnected to French post-St. Thome activities near Madras.
